patches.now: pip install --quiet dagster-dg-cli dagster && create-dagster project dagster-quickstart
patches.reason: The clean python:3.11-slim image has no Dagster installed, so the create-dagster executable doesn't exist. The create-dagster CLI is shipped by the dagster-dg-cli package (together with dagster), so installing it with pip puts it on PATH, and the original command then runs unchanged.

patches.was: pip install --quiet dagster-dg-cli dagster && create-dagster project dagster-quickstart
patches.now: pip install --quiet dagster-dg-cli dagster create-dagster && create-dagster project dagster-quickstart
patches.reason: The create-dagster executable ships in its own PyPI package, 'create-dagster', not in dagster-dg-cli or dagster. Installing only those two leaves the command missing, so the fix is to add create-dagster to the pip install. The pip root-user and upgrade messages are only warnings and can be ignored.

patches.now: python -m pip install --upgrade 'pip>=25.1' && python -m pip install --editable . --group dev
patches.reason: The --group option (PEP 735 dependency groups) was added in pip 25.1. The pip in the python:3.11-slim image is older and rejects it, so upgrading pip first should fix the error. I did not run this or search to confirm it.

proof.claim: A second clean container ran the patched steps with no model calls, and every step passed.
